The page's own Spanish never reaches the generator — it is only read to catch mismatches.
Three of its glosses are wrong and the correct English sense is asserted in the topic:
'slippers' are soft indoor shoes (pantuflas), not chanclas, which are flip-flops;
'waistband' is the band at the top of a pair of trousers, not a belt, and 'belt' sits in
the same unit so describing both as a belt would make them unanswerable against each
other; 'gown' is a long formal dress, not a bata. Each word was already in the unit its
real meaning belongs to, so only the definitions change.
Two words dropped. 'slacks' is a third word for pantalones and genuinely dated in American

This page is denser with collisions than any before it, and every pair sits in one unit:
PANTY-HOSE, SWEAT-SUIT and SWIM-SUIT normalised to their closed forms.

area.name: Clothes
area.description: Cómo se llama lo que te pones: camisas y pantalones, ropa formal, ropa interior, zapatos y todo lo que abriga.

units.name: Shirts and tops
units.topic: What you wear on the upper body every day, and the two general words for it. 'clothing' and 'clothes' are both ropa — clothing is the collective, slightly more formal word, clothes is what people actually say — and the unit should make that difference clear

units.name: Formal clothes
units.topic: What is worn to a wedding, an office or a formal evening. 'gown' here is a long formal dress worn to an important occasion. Its Spanish is 'vestido de gala' or 'vestido largo' — NEVER 'bata', which is a housecoat and a different garment entirely. 'dress' and 'gown' are both vestido and the unit should separate them: a dress is everyday, a gown is long and formal.

units.name: Trousers and skirts
units.topic: What you wear on the lower body and what holds it up. 'trousers' and 'pants' are the same garment — trousers is British, pants is American — and the unit should say so. 'waistband' is the band of cloth at the top of a pair of trousers or a skirt, NOT a belt: 'belt' is the separate strap you buy on its own, and the two are in this unit together so they must be described so they cannot be confused

units.name: Underwear
units.topic: What is worn under everything else. Several of these are close in meaning and the unit exists to separate them: 'underwear' is the general word, 'underpants' and 'panties' are specific garments, 'pantyhose' covers the legs and waist in one piece

units.name: Shoes and socks
units.topic: What goes on the feet, indoors and out. 'slippers' are the soft shoes worn inside the house — pantuflas — never open flip-flops. 'socks' and 'stockings' are both medias and the unit should separate them: socks reach the ankle or calf, stockings are thin and reach the thigh

units.name: Coats, hats and gloves
units.topic: What you put on when it is cold or when you go outside. 'gloves' and 'mittens' are both guantes and the difference is the point: gloves have a place for each finger, mittens keep the fingers together

units.name: Sport, swimming and storing clothes
units.topic: Clothes for exercise and the water, the cloth you carry in a pocket, and the piece of furniture clothes are kept in. 'trunks' are the shorts a man swims in. 'wardrobe' is ONLY the tall cupboard that clothes hang in — an armario or ropero. Do not define it as a person's collection of clothes; that sense is not taught here.
